approach: Add one reading-acceptance check, `check_scope_limit` in crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs, as a single `step!(check_scope_limit(reading));` line in `refusing_check` after `check_defined_terms` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. Root cause: nothing at the reading gate compares a scope limit with the files Athena always writes (CHANGELOG.md, forced by `ensure_changelog`, reading.rs:297) or with the readers of a changed config, so a limit written from the named files passes the gate and fails at verification (class scope-criterion-too-narrow-misses-dependent-tests; jobs 20261018-045437-7z81 and 20261023-052543-9bw7). A scope limit is a criterion for which `athena_context::briefs::limits_changed_files` (briefs.rs:146) is true, the same matcher that turns the deliverable list into the allowlist (`allowed_paths`, briefs.rs:115). The check applies to capability `change` readings with no question and does two things, both mechanical, with no scan of repo contents. (1) CHANGELOG half, revised after round 2: every limiting criterion is refused unless it names CHANGELOG.md (a default-written file, from a table built on `super::CHANGELOG_PATH`), points to 'the deliverables', or is a bare form that lists no exception (no whole word only/outside/except/beyond/besides/apart/aside/than), such as 'No other file is changed' or 'production unchanged'. So 'test-only change' and 'only the docs may change' are now refused even though they name no file. (2) Config half, revised: when a limiting criterion exists and athena.toml or defaults.toml is a deliverable, the reading must carry an assumption starting `Consumers:` that either names one or more crates/ paths, each of which is a deliverable (the deliverable list is the allowlist, so a consumer that is not listed would fail the scope guard as in 7z81), or says the file needs no change ('unchanged' or 'no change') or says the search found none ('none found'). The old shortcut 'any crates/ test deliverable satisfies the rule' is dropped. Support work: one READING_RULES line, unit tests in reading.rs, corpus cases with new input-form tags, a one-constant fix to the scope-test fixture LIMIT in run/tests.rs (forced), a CHANGELOG entry and decision D166.

decisions.choice: The CHANGELOG half applies to every criterion for which `limits_changed_files` is true. It is exempt only when the lowercased text contains 'changelog.md' (a name from the default-written table) or 'deliverable', or when the text is bare: it contains none of the whole words only, outside, except, beyond, besides, apart, aside, than (hyphens split words, as in the matcher). A CHANGELOG.md deliverable alone does not repair the limit text.
decisions.reason: `build_reading` calls `ensure_changelog` (reading.rs:859; definition 297-319) before `check_reading_acceptance` (reading.rs:680), so every change reading already lists CHANGELOG.md when the gate runs; a rule that accepted 'CHANGELOG.md listed' would never fire. The 9bw7 failure was a limit sentence that forbids the forced CHANGELOG edit. 'test-only change' and 'only the docs may change' (both matched by `limits_changed_files`, run_pin_tests.rs:1357-1358) forbid that edit just as much as a sentence naming a file, so the rule no longer waits for a named file (round 2, finding 2). A bare 'No other file is changed' lists no exception and stays accepted, as the critic asked.

rejected.option: Accept when CHANGELOG.md is a deliverable (the literal reading of criterion 2)
rejected.why: Inert for every production reading, so the class would stay open.

rejected.option: Fire only when the limit names a file (round 1 design)
rejected.why: Leaves 'test-only change' and 'only the docs may change' accepted although the job must still edit CHANGELOG.md; part of the class stays open.

rejected.option: Refuse a limit unless it lists every deliverable by name
rejected.why: Larger refusal rate than the evidence supports; 'the deliverables' is the existing way to point at the list.

decisions.choice: Only criteria are scanned; out_of_scope items are not. The limit matcher is `limits_changed_files`, imported from athena_context::briefs; the exception-word test is a small private helper.
decisions.reason: One definition for the gate and for verification-time enforcement (`limiting_criterion` reads criteria only, briefs.rs:103-108), so the gate cannot drift from what is enforced. out_of_scope items are exclusions, never an allowlist, and 'files kept from job X' would cause false refusals. This departs from the reading's 'criterion or out_of_scope item'; raised as a User question.

rejected.option: A new phrase list ('only', 'nothing else', 'no other') as the trigger in checks.rs
rejected.why: A second matcher that would drift from `limits_changed_files`.
Enforcement ignores them, and exclusions would cause false refusals.

decisions.choice: The config half fires only with a limiting criterion (exempt or not) and a deliverable whose normalized path is athena.toml or defaults.toml. It is met only by a `Consumers:` assumption (trimmed, any case, like `code_surveys` in surveys.rs:116) in one of three forms: (a) it names crates/ paths (words containing `crates/` with quotes, backticks and end punctuation trimmed, checked with `names_crates_path`, surveys.rs:127) and every such path equals a deliverable path or lies under a deliverable that ends in '/'; (b) the same line says 'unchanged' or 'no change'; (c) the line says 'none found'. A Consumers line that names no crates/ path and says neither is refused.
decisions.reason: With a limit the deliverable list is the allowlist (briefs.rs:110-126). In 20261018-045437-7z81 the tests that load the real athena.toml were not deliverables, so the scope guard failed the job. The 7z81 introspection's prevention was that the reading should then allow those files; requiring each named consumer to be a deliverable does exactly that (round 2, finding 3). Form (c) lets a reader state a search result of none; the check cannot verify the search and D166 says so.

rejected.option: Accept any crates/ test deliverable as the answer (round 1)
rejected.why: An unrelated test deliverable such as refusal_corpus.rs satisfied the rule without any search or without widening the allowlist to the real consumers.

rejected.option: Accept a Consumers line that names crates/ paths that are not deliverables
rejected.why: The producer would have to edit them and the scope guard would fail the job as in 7z81.

rejected.option: Scan repo content for files that load the config
rejected.why: Out of scope; readers see a plain copy and the gate must stay deterministic.

rejected.option: Require the consumer rule for every config deliverable, even without a limit
rejected.why: Without a limit the producer may touch consumers freely; refuses readings that cannot suffer the failure.

decisions.choice: Default-written files go in a const table `DEFAULT_WRITTEN_FILES: [(&str, &str); 1]` whose only row is (`super::CHANGELOG_PATH`, reason text), and config files in `CONFIG_FILES: [&str; 2]`, both in checks.rs.
decisions.reason: `CHANGELOG_PATH` (reading.rs:293) is the constant `ensure_changelog` writes; checks.rs is a child module of reading and already has `use super::*` (checks.rs:3), so the gate and the writer share one source (round 2, finding 4). The table follows the convention of GOVERNANCE_BY_DELIVERABLE; the reason text feeds the error; a future default file is one row.

rejected.option: Hard-code the string CHANGELOG.md in the logic or a second literal in the table
rejected.why: Can drift from what ensure_changelog writes and loses the reason text.

risks.risk: False refusals: `limits_changed_files` matches a criterion that mentions a limit in passing (for example 'test-only change in the checks table'), and the broader CHANGELOG half now refuses such limits too.
risks.mitigation: The matcher already errs toward not matching (briefs.rs:140-145). The repair is one phrase ('and CHANGELOG.md' or 'the deliverables'), given in the error text. Bare forms ('No other file is changed', 'production unchanged') stay accepted and are pinned by corpus Accept cases. The replay measures the share, declared as an estimate.

risks.risk: The Consumers rule cannot verify that the search was done: a line `Consumers: none found` or one naming deliverables can be written without searching, and the exception-word test is a word list that can miss a limit phrased with another word.
risks.mitigation: D166 states the limit: the gate forces the question and checks that every named consumer is a deliverable; scanning repo content is out of scope. An unlisted consumer that the reader names is caught; one it does not name is the remaining gap and is named in D166.

risks.risk: The new READING_RULES line pushes a rule line past 220 bytes or the section past its bound.
risks.mitigation: Keep the line to about 200 bytes; if the section exceeds the bound, set the bound to the measured size plus a small margin and fix its comment. `cargo test -p athena-context` shows it. The reader prompt is untouched, so no budget line in system-facts.md changes.

risks.risk: Another test or fake reader outside the places found pushes a limit phrase through the gate and starts failing.
risks.mitigation: Step 9 runs `cargo test --locked` for the whole workspace. A failing fixture gets 'and CHANGELOG.md' in its limit text, as LIMIT does; the check is not weakened.

risks.risk: run/tests.rs is not among the six listed deliverables, so a scope guard built from this job's deliverable list could flag it.
risks.mitigation: The edit is one constant under crates/ (the request's Files scope), listed in `files`, raised as a User open question, and checked by criterion 8's `git diff --stat`. Exempting README.md-only limits in the check was rejected as a hole in the rule.

risks.risk: A Consumers line naming a path under a directory deliverable, a `./` prefix, quotes or backticks is mis-parsed and refused.
risks.mitigation: Trim `./`, quotes, backticks and end punctuation as `allowed_paths` does (briefs.rs:119-120); a deliverable ending in '/' covers paths under it; corpus and unit cases pin both forms.
